clue.text: What you get having left artist to it

definitions.text: What you get having left artist to it

parts.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's stock artist

explanation.surface: Sitting for a painter, you leave the job to the artist and see what you end up with.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR turned 'it' into '11'; the page prints 'it'. The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: leave the artist to it and a painting of you results.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted likeness is the result a sitter receives once the painter has finished working on them.

clue.text: Touching way to call up

parts.note: a path is a way or track

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word for call is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to cite is to call or summon, as a witness to court

explanation.surface: A moving way to summon someone upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Touching in the sense of stirring pity, as a sad story moves the heart.

clue.text: Fix mother up with a part in a rambling exposition

parts.note: to rig is to fix or fiddle, as with a rigged election
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: Someone sets up their mother with a stage part, then talks endlessly about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix ... up' together means RIG, as in rig up; 'up' is left as part of that phrasal verb and supplies nothing further.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, confused and wandering account is a lengthy palaver, the sense of this word.

clue.text: Tangent, perhaps, right at one 'circle

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a circle has the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A geometry lesson: a tangent line, drawn on the right, touching a circle at one point.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray mark before 'circle' is a printing speck. 'Tangent' is the trigonometric function, not the touching line the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: In trigonometry the tangent is the quotient of opposite over adjacent sides, an example of a proportion between quantities.

clue.text: Metrically opposite

definitions.meaning: written metrically means set in poetry
contrary, turned the other way round, as an inverted ratio

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means written as poetry; as one word it means reversed or contrary.

clue.text: Its act suffers interference

indicators.note: the words its act are knocked about and damaged, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer's routine is spoiled by someone butting in.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackling noise on a radio or television signal is electrical interference.

clue.text: 7 fish running slowly

parts.note: the answer to 7 Down, a word meaning spell
ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A fish moves slowly through a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that flows in a thin, slow stream is said to dribble or seep along.

clue.text: Spell "patron" without the PA

indicators.note: without tells us that the letters of PA are taken away from the patron's name

parts.note: Saint Patrick is the patron saint of Ireland
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to write out a word with two letters omitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patron' is in quotation marks to make it look like the word itself, but it stands for the patron saint, Patrick.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor's spell or turn at the helm is called a trick; both words mean a shift of duty.

clue.text: Frank and I enrolled in the Diplomatic Corps

indicators.note: being enrolled in a body means going inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: CD stands for Corps Diplomatique, the diplomatic corps

explanation.surface: A man named Frank and I joined the diplomatic service together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frank means being open and honest in speech.

clue.text: A game of pontoon?

definitions.meaning: a card game for four players in two partnerships
a pontoon is a floating structure carrying a road across water

explanation.surface: Asking whether a certain card game counts as pontoon.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon is itself a card game (blackjack), which makes the surface ask about cards; here it is the floating crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a card game for two pairs and a structure spanning a river, as a pontoon one does.

clue.text: Firm hampered by lack 'of money

definitions.meaning: firm as in fixed fast, secure
short of cash, as when money is said to be scarce

explanation.surface: A company held back because it is short of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The mark before 'of' is a printing speck.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fastened securely and, of funds, scarce or hard to come by.

clue.text: With pests around, 17 turns red

indicators.note: around says the pests' word goes round the other piece

parts.note: vermin are pests such as rats and mice

indicators.note: turns means the word for 17 is read backwards

parts.note: the answer to 17 Down means to make slippery, which is to oil

explanation.surface: Surrounded by vermin, something goes red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses OIL to LIO, which 'around' puts inside VERMIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant scarlet pigment, so a vivid shade of that colour.

clue.text: Losing your head you meander, madly in love

indicators.note: madly tells us the remaining letters are wildly rearranged
the head of the word you is its first letter, and losing it removes it

explanation.surface: Advice that wandering about distractedly is what being besotted does to you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing your head' removes Y from YOU MEANDER; 'madly' rearranges what is left, OUMEANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone smitten is captivated by another person.

clue.text: The sword brought back distress to this country

indicators.note: brought back means the combined pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: to irk is to annoy or distress
for a British paper, this country is the UK

explanation.surface: A sword brought home caused distress in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns the whole of IRK + UK. The definition is a Gurkha's curved knife.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved Nepalese blade carried by Gurkha soldiers is a short sword or large knife.

clue.text: Detach one note, its successors follow

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
so (or soh) is the fifth note of the tonic sol-fa scale
after so in the sol-fa scale come la and te

explanation.surface: A music lesson: pick out one note and let the following ones come after.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate something and keep it apart from others is to detach it.

clue.text: PM comes out of No. Ten, for a change

indicators.note: for a change signals that the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister emerges from Number Ten Downing Street for some variety.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister, who lives at No. 10 Downing Street, London; here it is post meridiem. NOTEN + FORA are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: PM, post meridiem, marks the hours after midday.

clue.text: Foodstuff belied its ingredients

definitions.note: a noun here; the answer serves as a noun in the plural form edibles

indicators.note: the ingredients are the component letters of belied, mixed up as in a recipe

explanation.surface: A food that gave a false picture of what went into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything fit to be eaten counts as food; the word is used as a noun for comestibles.

clue.text: Built with care, contrived to reduce friction

indicators.note: contrived means put together artificially, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something carefully constructed and cleverly designed to cut down rubbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying oil or grease to moving parts makes them slide smoothly.

clue.text: Story arose about a penny once paid for protection

indicators.note: about means the reversed story goes round the next letter
in a down answer arose means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a legend is a traditional story
d was the abbreviation for an old British penny

explanation.surface: A tale grew up about a penny once spent on security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arose' turns LEGEND to DNEGEL, 'about' puts A inside it, and the old penny D follows. D was the symbol for a penny before British decimal coinage in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval English kings raised a tax to buy off Viking raiders; it was tribute paid to keep them away.

clue.text: The right breed of cattle

definitions.meaning: in heraldry, the right-hand side of a shield as its bearer sees it
a small hardy Irish breed of cattle

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the heraldic term for the right side and the name of a small Irish cattle breed.

clue.text: Rag and bone man gives up name in return for tatter

parts.note: to rag is to tease, which is to rib

indicators.note: gives up means the following letters are removed from the words bone man
in return means the word name is read backwards

explanation.surface: A junk dealer swaps his name for a scrap of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' turns NAME into EMAN, and 'gives up' removes that run from BONEMAN, leaving BON. A rag-and-bone man is a British street collector of old junk.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn cloth hanging in strips is said to be in shreds, so a tatter is a strip of torn fabric.

clue.text: Conclusions of 27 common in system of calculation

annotationWithheld.why: Conclusions of 27 common in system of calculation (7): 27 is ORTHODOXY here, and no reading of its conclusions plus 'common' gives ALGEBRA; the cross-reference looks wrong as held
annotationWithheld.clue: Conclusions of 27 common in system of calculation

clue.text: A senior officer, yet somehow an inferior one

parts.note: Col is short for colonel, a senior army officer

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of yet are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A senior officer who is nonetheless lower in rank.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant or junior attendant, especially one serving a priest, is a follower of lower standing.

clue.text: Give some relief; showing me up before master

indicators.note: before places the reversed word ahead of the master
in a down answer up means the word me is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a boss is a master or employer

explanation.surface: Showing a superior that I can help ease the strain.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a design so that it stands out from a surface is to work it in relief.

clue.text: Officer about to quit island

indicators.note: to quit means the letters for about leave the island's name

parts.note: Majorca is the largest Balearic island
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: An army officer is about to leave an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is not a link here but circa, CA.
explanation.definitionFit: An army rank above captain and below lieutenant colonel.

clue.text: Black mole

definitions.meaning: jet-black, as dark as the mineral jet
a mole is a stone pier or breakwater

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means as dark as jet; as a noun it is a landing pier, like a harbour mole.

clue.text: Guns fired from E. Anglian shore

parts.note: a broad is one of the Norfolk Broads, lakes in East Anglia
the seaside is the shore

explanation.surface: Cannon fire comes from the coast of eastern England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are a network of lakes in East Anglia, eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A warship firing all the cannon on one side at once delivers a simultaneous volley.

clue.text: Two score

definitions.meaning: the two in a pack of cards or on a die
the tennis score of forty all

explanation.definitionFit: It is the card or die face showing a pair of pips and the tied tennis score at forty all.

clue.text: Soundness of heart of musketeer and paramour

indicators.note: heart of means only the middle of the musketeer's name is kept

parts.note: Porthos is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers
a doxy is a mistress or lover

explanation.surface: A judgment on the integrity of a musketeer and his lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' drops P and S from PORTHOS to leave ORTHO.
explanation.definitionFit: Soundness of belief, adherence to accepted doctrine, is correctness of opinion.

clue.text: America, for instance, rejected this practice

parts.note: USA is the United States of America

indicators.note: rejected means the abbreviation is turned back on itself

parts.note: eg is short for exempli gratia, for instance

explanation.surface: The United States, for example, turned down this custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Customary practice is the habitual way something is done.

clue.text: Saw an unknown participating in chant

indicators.note: participating in means the pair goes inside the word for chant

parts.note: to sing is to chant
an gives the letter A
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns, so Y

explanation.surface: Someone saw a stranger joining in with the singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb, a familiar maxim.

clue.text: The right girl to split on the vicar

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
to rend is to split or tear apart

explanation.surface: The ideal girl to break up with the clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reverend is the title used for a vicar or other member of the clergy.
